title: Network-Hosted PowerShell Execution With Destructive Script Content

detection_logic.summary: Correlates network-hosted PowerShell process creation using suspicious execution options with PowerShell operational content containing destructive filesystem-operation categories on the same host within five minutes.

evidence_references.label: attack
evidence_references.relevance: The normalized process-creation record contains data.event_id 1, data.process_image ending in powershell.exe, a UNC path in data.command_line, and suspicious execution options.

evidence_references.label: attack
evidence_references.relevance: The normalized PowerShell operational record contains data.event_id 4103 and data.script_text with Remove-Item.

evidence_references.label: baseline
evidence_references.relevance: The normalized baseline PowerShell record is Event ID 4103 but its data.script_text does not contain a proposed destructive filesystem-operation category.

expected_attack_result.expected_behavior: Expected to generate a high-confidence correlation when both components occur on the same host within 300 seconds; a single matched component is expected to be assigned medium confidence.

expected_baseline_result.expected_behavior: Expected to produce no matches where baseline records do not satisfy both the network-hosted suspicious PowerShell component and destructive PowerShell-content component.

limitations: PowerShell Event IDs 4103 and 4104 depend on logging configuration and may be absent.
Host-and-time correlation can combine unrelated activity when process identifiers are unavailable across sources.
Destructive PowerShell filesystem commands and network-hosted PowerShell can be legitimate administrative or maintenance activity.
This rule does not use RDP attribution as detection proof.

deployment_target.description: Windows machine running the Project Janus Python scripts
